body: Difficulty Communicating (Online Multiplayer):

{Bullet}For planning and discussing strategy, Spirits may not use any language shared in common, and may not look at each others' Power Cards in the Spirit Phase. (Once the {Fast} phase starts, played cards become visible.){EndBullet}
{Bullet}A limited set of emoticons is available via text chat.{EndBullet}
{Bullet}Planning markers may be used as usual.{EndBullet}
{Bullet}When performing game effects not associated with a particular Spirit, player, or board, individual Spirits are assigned to make decisions, instead of voting.{EndBullet}
{Bullet}Roleplaying is not required, but can add to the atmosphere if your group enjoys such things.{EndBullet}

{Bullet}Players may not normally control more than one Spirit in this Scenario. If you end up controlling multiple Spirits due to a disconnection, do your best to act as if your Spirits are limited as intended.{EndBullet}
Difficulty Coordinating (Multihanded Solo):
{Bullet}You may only view one Spirit at a time, and while doing so, you may not look at any information pertaining to the other Spirits.{EndBullet}
{Bullet}In the Spirit Phase, you must perform the whole phase for each Spirit, one at a time, in a randomly determined order.{EndBullet}

{Bullet}In the {Fast} and {Slow} Phases, one at a time, a Spirit is randomly chosen to use a Power, use a Special Rule, or gain a flexible Element (or pass and take no more actions), until all actions are used or all Spirits pass.{EndBullet}

body: Strength in Diversity
After Growth, if you added 1 or more {Presence} to lands with another Spirits' {Presence}: Gain 1 Energy or Reclaim 1 non-Major Power Card.

ADiversityOfSpirits.flavorText: Why should a Spirit of the open air speak the same language as a Spirit of flame and renewal or understand the deep voice of a mountain? The Spirits defending the island are strong in their own nature and have difficulty communicating nuanced information to each other as a result.

body: {Bullet}This Scenario is less about mechanical changes and more about altering the experience of the game. Some players love it, but it's not for everyone.{EndBullet}

body: This Scenario can be fun for anyone to try, but is particularly meant for players who find they prefer a more play-and-resolve style of game to the planning ahead required by Spirits' {Slow} Powers.
All Powers are {Fast}.
Powers which were already {Fast} (or made {Fast}) cost 1 less Energy. (For Innate Powers and Power Cards costing 0, instead gain 1 Energy.)
When Exploring, once per board, add an additional {Explorer}.
If the Island becomes “Blighted”, put 1 less {Blight} per starting board on the Blight Card.
